newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Iran resistance urges tough EU stand on Iran.
newsitem.headline: Iran resistance urges tough EU stand on Iran.

text.p: Several hundred demonstrators from Iran's resistance movement, with banners waving and Iranian music blasting out over loudspeakers, urged EU foreign ministers on Tuesday to end their critical dialogue with Iran.

The demonstrators, chanting in the drizzle and against the backdrop of a red banner reading "to tolerate terrorism is to encourage it" also called on the EU to sever all diplomatic and trade links with Iran.

"It's nothing but to demand an end to the critical dialogue once and for all," Zohre Akhyani, representative for the National Council of Resistance of Iran in Germany, told Reuters in front of the building where EU ministers met.

Rather than ending the dialogue, EU foreign ministers looked set on Tuesday to send ambassadors from their 15 nations back to Iran, almost three weeks after withdrawing them in protest at alleged state involvement in murder.
They were withdrawn on April 10 after a German court ruled that Iran's government had been involved in the murder in Berlin of Kurdish Iranian opposition leaders.
Akhyani said that sending the EU ambassadors back to Tehran would "simply encourage more terrorism."
The EU's 'critical dialogue' was based on the view that it was better to keep open communications with Iran than to isolate it.
The diplomat said the move was a political gesture reflecting the European Union's determination to fight terrorism in all its forms.

"This is confirmation of the EU's condemnation of state inspired acts of terrorism. With this show of solidarity the EU is capable of delivering a coordinated follow-up (to withdrawing its ambassadors on April 10)," he said.

According to a draft of the ministers' agreement, the EU will also continue its arms embargo on Iran, will not grant visa to Iranians with intelligence or security functions and will move to exclude all Iranian intelligence personnel from the European Union.
"Under present circumstances...there is no basis for continuing critical dialogue with Iran," the draft said.
